evals.prompt: I'm building an ASP.NET Core minimal API and want to pull secrets from AWS Secrets Manager into IConfiguration named "prod/myapp/db". How do I wire this up?
evals.expected_output: Adds the AWSSecretsManager.Provider NuGet package, calls builder.Configuration.AddSecretsManager(...) on the WebApplicationBuilder (optionally with a logger/loggerFactory overload), and explains that with no AcceptedSecretArns/filters set it will list and fetch every accessible secret rather than only the named one, suggesting AcceptedSecretArns or SecretFilter to scope it to that secret.
assertions: Uses a real AddSecretsManager overload signature (no logger, ILogger<SecretsManagerConfigurationProvider>, or ILoggerFactory)
Does not claim a logger is automatically resolved from DI without an explicit overload
Mentions scoping to the specific secret via AcceptedSecretArns or SecretFilter rather than leaving it fetching everything

evals.prompt: I have about 40 secrets I need loaded efficiently, want them refreshed every 5 minutes without restarting the app, and want all the resulting configuration keys upper-cased. What options do I need?
evals.expected_output: Sets UseBatchFetch=true (and notes the secretsmanager:BatchGetSecretValue IAM permission requirement and the 20-secret-per-request chunking), sets PollingInterval=TimeSpan.FromMinutes(5) for background reload, and sets KeyGenerator=(entry,key)=>key.ToUpper() for uppercasing.
assertions: Sets UseBatchFetch to true and mentions the 20-secret batch chunk limit
Mentions the secretsmanager:BatchGetSecretValue IAM permission is required
Sets PollingInterval to enable background reload rather than suggesting a manual restart
Sets KeyGenerator to uppercase the key rather than inventing an unrelated casing option

evals.prompt: One of my secrets is a JSON blob like {"ConnectionStrings":{"Primary":"..."}} stored under the name MyDb. How do I read the Primary connection string from IConfiguration, and does the casing of the key matter?
evals.expected_output: Explains the secret is recursively flattened using ':'-delimited ConfigurationPath keys, so the value is readable at configuration["MyDb:ConnectionStrings:Primary"], and that key lookups are case-insensitive so casing does not matter.
assertions: Correctly describes ':'-delimited flattening producing the key MyDb:ConnectionStrings:Primary
States that configuration key lookups are case-insensitive
Does not claim Newtonsoft/JSON.NET or a different delimiter is used

evals.prompt: I set IgnoreMissingValues=true and UseBatchFetch=true, but I'm still getting an AggregateException with a DecryptionFailureException inside it. Isn't IgnoreMissingValues supposed to prevent errors like this?
evals.expected_output: Explains that IgnoreMissingValues only suppresses errors when every error in a batch is a missing-secret (ResourceNotFoundException) error; a DecryptionFailureException or other non-missing error type in the same batch still throws an AggregateException regardless of IgnoreMissingValues, and suggests inspecting AggregateException.InnerExceptions to see which secrets failed and why (likely a KMS key permission or state issue for that decryption failure specifically).
assertions: Correctly explains IgnoreMissingValues only suppresses all-missing-secret batches, not all error types
Explicitly names DecryptionFailureException as a non-missing-secret error type that still throws
Does not claim this is a bug or that IgnoreMissingValues should be expected to suppress it

evals.prompt: For local development I want to point this at a LocalStack container instead of real AWS, and I'd also like some console log output showing when secrets load without setting up full dependency injection logging.
evals.expected_output: Uses ConfigureSecretsManagerConfig to set ServiceURL (and UseHttp) to the LocalStack endpoint with dummy/basic credentials, and separately passes an ILoggerFactory (e.g. LoggerFactory.Create(lb => lb.AddConsole())) directly to the AddSecretsManager loggerFactory overload rather than assuming DI wires it automatically.
assertions: Uses ConfigureSecretsManagerConfig with ServiceURL (or ServiceUrl) pointed at a local endpoint for LocalStack, not CreateClient bypassing it unnecessarily
Explicitly passes an ILoggerFactory or ILogger to an AddSecretsManager overload rather than claiming automatic DI-based logger resolution
Does not claim a dedicated first-class LocalStack integration package exists

evals.prompt: A secret I created is just not appearing anywhere in my IConfiguration, no exception, nothing. What could cause this?
evals.expected_output: Lists binary secrets (SecretBinary set with no SecretString) as silently skipped with no error as one likely cause, and a SecretFilter or AcceptedSecretArns scope excluding it as another; does not claim the provider throws in either case.
assertions: Mentions binary secrets (SecretBinary-only, no SecretString) are silently skipped as a candidate cause
Mentions SecretFilter or AcceptedSecretArns scoping as another candidate cause
Does not claim the provider would throw an exception in either of these cases
